statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-107884: kadmind's password change server did not check the lockdown_keys attribute before changing a principal's keys. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3 (https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html; commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2515fb5d3d8eb3577ea60cd14d7216c654718597). Alpine lists it under 1.22.3-r0 in the 3.23-stable main/krb5 APKBUILD secfixes (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/krb5/APKBUILD). This owner's published builds for Alpine 3.23 are 1.22.1-r0, built from an earlier MIT release, which is affected, and 1.22.3-r0, built from the MIT 1.22.3 release, which is fixed.

CVE-2026-107884 (kadmind's password change server did not check the lockdown_keys attribute before changing a principal's keys) is fixed upstream in krb5 1.22.3 (https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html; commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/2515fb5d3d8eb3577ea60cd14d7216c654718597) and is unfixed in Debian trixie (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-107884). This owner backports the fix onto Debian's 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 in its current build, whose shipped package changelog records it; the earlier builds of that Debian version do not carry it. Pending: two retired builds of Debian's 1.21.3-5 from an earlier versioning scheme, published before the backport and so without the fix, still appear in this request and sort above the fixed build under Debian version ordering, so no version range can mark them affected while marking the current build fixed. The status will be set once the request is reissued against the builds currently published.
